messages:
ivy-support: Escalation — customer (private VPC) reported API errors after they rotated their IPsec pre-shared key and CA around 14:12 UTC. Tunnels show as UP from our side but traffic to private endpoints times out. Examples: curl to private-api returns 'TLS handshake timeout' and pings fail.

raj_net: Can you paste ipsec status and any tcpdump snippets? Also confirm whether UDP 500/4500 were allowed on their firewall after the rotation.

ivy-support: Paste from their telemetry (redacted):
```
# ipsec statusall
Status of IKE charon daemon (strongSwan 5.9.4):
  uptime: 2 minutes, since Apr 14 14:14:22
  security associations (1 up, 1 connecting):
  aes256-sha256-modp2048: 192.0.2.44[4500]->198.51.100.9[4500] (established)
  conn 'redwood-prod': INSTALLED, TUNNEL, ESP in use
  child 'redwood-prod-internal': INSTALLED, reqid 1, traffic selectors LOCAL: 10.10.0.0/24 REMOTE: 10.20.0.0/24
```

ivy-support: And tcpdump on our egress shows ESP but no inner IPs visible (looks like encrypted traffic arriving):
```
14:15:02.123456 IP 198.51.100.9.4500 > 192.0.2.44.4500: UDP, length 152
14:15:02.123789 IP 198.51.100.9 > 192.0.2.44: ESP(spi=0x5f3a1b2c)
# no IKE notifications or NAT-T revisits after 14:12
```

samir_oncall: Two quick checks: 1) Confirm IKE proposals (cipher/auth) match end-to-end — if customer rotated PSK but also flipped IKE profile to require RSA certs the SA might look 'INSTALLED' but child SA could be failing application-level. 2) Ensure UDP 500/4500 and ESP are allowed both directions — some appliances create temporary deny rules on rotation.

maria_eng: Note that this private deployment also validates client certs for certain calls (mTLS). Our logs show TLS verify errors in the private agent around the same time:
```
2026-04-14T14:13:01Z private-agent ERROR tls: remote cert verification failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
2026-04-14T14:13:02Z private-agent WARN connection: handshake failed for 10.20.0.5:443
```
That implies CA rotation on the customer side without updating trust stores for service certs.

ivy-support: Customer notes: they rotated PSK and CA on their edge appliance at 14:12 and claim they updated the PSK on their side. They did not mention updating internal service truststores.

raj_net: If PSK was mismatched we'd usually see IKE rekey errors. The 'INSTALLED' state suggests IKE completed but the child ESP might be failing or policy routing is wrong. Can you run a quick "ip xfrm state" and "ip route show table main" on the appliance (ask customer) and confirm no accidental policy change? Also verify their phase2 uses the same transform (esp aes256gcm?).

ivy-support: Asked them for: ip xfrm, ip route, full strongSwan debug logs, and appliance audit showing the PSK update step. Also asked them to run a capture for inner traffic.

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026 and paged oncall.

samir_oncall: Short-term mitigations to propose to customer:
- Roll back the PSK rotation on the appliance if they can (fastest).
- If rollback impossible, re-provision PSK again and confirm both sides have identical strings (watch for hidden characters/newline issues).
- For the mTLS break, add our private CA to their truststore or temporarily disable client cert verification for smoke tests.
- Ensure their firewall doesn't apply implicit outbound deny rules after config changes (ask them to whitelist our public egress IPs).

maria_eng: I'll create a small runbook note: when PSK + CA rotate in same window, check IKE/ESP separately and check application TLS verification. Add a check that flags 'x509 verify failed' in agent logs as a high-priority alert tied to private VPC customers.

ivy-support: Customer returned appliance logs — they had a PSK sync, but the management UI appended a trailing space to the PSK value when saving ("secret123 ") — common gotcha. After we told them to re-enter without trailing whitespace, IKE rekey progressed and inner traffic came up. They also pushed the CA cert into their internal services truststores which fixed the mTLS errors.

raj_net: Happy path confirmation steps we asked them to run:
1) from a host in their remote LAN: curl -v https://10.20.0.5:443/health -> should return 200 and show cert chain with our CA.
2) on their appliance: `ipsec statusall` should show child INSTALLED and `ip xfrm state` should show active ESP SAs.
3) tcpdump on our egress should show decrypted inner traffic once ESP is processed by xfrm (we should see inner src/dst 10.10.0.x/10.20.0.x).

ivy-support: Customer confirmed tests passed post-fix; API calls started succeeding at 14:43 UTC. Closing loop here but leaving notes for dev/product to add better visibility and a sanity-check that flags PSK saves with trailing whitespace and CA rotations for Private customers.

maria_eng: Filing a follow-up PR for runbook and a small UX note to teammates to validate PSK entry widget trims whitespace by default.

ivy-support: Thanks team — will add postmortem summary to the incident channel and update the private deployment checklist.
